findings.title: Legacy SQL command construction path is not explicitly disabled
findings.body: UnmarshalSQLCommand still accepts a raw SQL expression and calls NewSQLCommand without any disabled/feature check. It currently fails only incidentally because sql.TablesList calls the stub DB's RunCommands and NewSQLCommand maps that 'not implemented' error to a BadRequest for invalid SQL. The kill switch is therefore not enforced at this entry point, produces a misleading error, and restoring a working DB/parser implementation would remove the only construction barrier on this path even though SQL expressions are supposed to be disabled. Add an explicit disabled check to UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand or remove those constructors while the feature is disabled.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false through inverted dead logic
findings.body: The helper computes enabled as the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false both inside the if and after it, so the feature toggle has no effect and the logic reads as the opposite of its name. It also unnecessarily dereferences h.features: a reader constructed with nil toggles will panic on a SQL query instead of returning the intended disabled error. Replace this with an explicit unconditional disabled return with a comment, or implement the toggle check without negation.

findings.title: No regression test covers the SQL-expression kill switch
findings.body: This security change makes the reader reject SQL expressions and makes NewSQLCommand/TablesList/Execute fail through the stub DB, but no _test.go file is changed. Add tests proving that a SQL expression is rejected when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled through ReadQuery, that the raw-node UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand path cannot construct an executable command, and that Execute returns an error rather than running the query; otherwise a future refactor or DB restoration could silently re-enable the CVE-2024-9264 vulnerable path.
